idea.title: Washio: on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning pickup by app

source.text: Washio: on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning pickup and delivery ordered by app, launch country US. Score it as of 2013-06-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a seed-funded startup. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug washio.

idea.problem: Doing laundry and getting to a dry cleaner during opening hours takes time busy urban people don't have.
idea.solution: A smartphone app to order on-demand pickup and delivery of laundry and dry cleaning.
claims: on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning pickup and delivery ordered by app
assumptions: Founder is a seed-funded team (stated); budget assumed to be a typical 2013 seed round, about USD 0.5-1.5M.
Launch city assumed to be Los Angeles; target customer assumed to be urban professionals without in-unit washers.
Operating model assumed outsourced: partner cleaners do the cleaning, contractor drivers do pickup and delivery.
Price assumed $1.75/lb wash & fold, 15-lb orders, $0.85/lb wholesale, 0.5 driver-hour per order (no dated 2012 LA prices found).
Scored as of 2013-06-01 with no questions asked (headless run): sources published after that date were excluded.

confidence.note: Unit economics rest on assumed price/lb, wholesale cost and route density; a dated 2012 LA price list and pilot data would raise it.

gross_margin.note: Est. 17% gross margin per 15-lb order after partner wholesale, LA driver wage and card fees; kill shot costs_eat_margin (R5 <= 2).

ltv_cac.note: Est. LTV $54 (12 orders x $4.51) vs CAC ~$27.50 from Facebook CPC: ~2.0, thin but positive.

pricing_power.note: Cleaners like 1-800-DryClean already deliver free, so a convenience premium is hard to charge.

build_effort.note: Booking app plus one partner cleaner; a concierge SMS version can run in about a week.

skills_match.note: Seed team assumed to cover app build; logistics and dispatch ops are the unproven half.

capital_needed.note: Seed round covers a city pilot, but MyLackey burned $8M in 16 months on errand logistics.

time_to_mvp.note: Manual pickups with one partner cleaner can take paid orders in 1-2 weeks.

sales_cycle.note: Consumer impulse purchase: order tonight, pay by card, no committee.

channel_readiness.note: Channels exist (Facebook, give-get referrals like Uber) but no audience yet and real CAC unknown.

search_demand.note: ~42,000 US cleaning establishments and ~$20.4B receipts (2002 Census): a mass, weekly need.

trend.note: No pre-2013 dated trend found for cleaning spend; treated as flat. Smartphone adoption rising.

willingness_to_pay.note: People already pay for cleaning ($22B est.); paying extra for delivery is unproven.

free_alternatives.note: Home washers and cleaners' free delivery cover part of the job; dry cleaning still needs a pro.

competitor_density.note: Few direct players pre-June 2013: SpotlessCity ($200k seed, NYC), Laundry Locker, Exec.

differentiation.note: App-first on-demand timing is real but copyable; cleaners already deliver free.

legal_regulatory.note: Estrada v. FedEx (CA, 2007): contractor drivers held employees; 'ninja' drivers carry that risk.

platform_dependency.note: iOS app, but services are paid outside Apple IAP (no 30% cut); web booking is an alternative.

market_risk.note: Laundry is a durable, recurring weekly need, not a fad.

skills.note: Seed-funded team; operating track record in logistics unknown (assumption).

assets.note: Capital is the only stated asset: no audience, data or cleaner contracts.

interest.note: Motivation not stated; assumed curious, not domain passion.

tam.reasoning: $20.4B employer receipts (2002 Census via American Laundry News) + ~$2.0B nonemployer receipts (2007, Statistical Abstract 2012); different years, rough sum

sam.reasoning: 10% of TAM: urban smartphone-owning households in dense metros (assumption; 46% of adults own smartphones, Pew 2012)

som.reasoning: 0.1% of SAM in year 1 for one-city launch (LA)

competitors_found.reasoning: Named pre-June-2013: SpotlessCity, Laundry Locker, 1-800-DryClean, Exec, plus local cleaners with delivery

price.reasoning: 15 lb wash & fold x $1.75/lb (assumed order size and price; no dated 2012 LA price found)

expected_lifetime.reasoning: assumption: ~6 months at 2 orders/month before churn; no pre-2013 benchmark

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: assumed click-to-first-order rate for a local consumer service

ltv.reasoning: 12 orders x $4.51 gross profit per order

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: assumption: 4-person seed team at ~$8k loaded each + $8k tools, insurance, office

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 40,000 / (2 orders x $4.51) per active customer per month

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: concierge pilot: landing page + SMS ordering + one partner cleaner

verdict.launch_reason: Stated launch country; LA density and smartphone adoption (46% of US adults, 2012) support a one-city pilot.
verdict.cheapest_test: 7-day concierge pilot in one dense LA zip code: landing page, SMS ordering, one partner cleaner, founders drive; measure orders per driver-hour and margin.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 30 paid orders in the pilot zip code by day 7 -> stop
Fewer than 2 orders per driver-hour by day 14 -> stop scaling, redesign routes
Repeat rate under 30% of first-time customers by day 30 -> stop
Gross profit under USD 6 per order by day 30 -> raise price or stop

rescue.change: Lead with dry cleaning in 2-3 dense LA zip codes, add a flat $5.99 delivery fee and batch pickups into fixed time windows.
rescue.why: Raises gross_margin and ltv_cac (costs_eat_margin): est. 3 orders per driver-hour lifts margin toward 35-40%.
rescue.effort: 2-3 months of route and pricing tests
rescue.requires: Dispatch software, density data, a partner cleaner with volume pricing

rescue.change: Sell through luxury apartment buildings and office perk programs (Exec-style company accounts) instead of paid ads.
rescue.why: Fixes channel_readiness and route density (liquidity): one building = many orders per stop, lower CAC.
rescue.requires: Property-manager intros, a concierge drop box

rescue.change: Own a small processing plant instead of paying partner wholesale.
rescue.why: Captures the cleaner's margin (gross_margin), but raises capital_needed and execution risk.

type_checks.note: Supply (cleaners with spare capacity) is easy; no pre-2013 benchmark for orders per neighborhood needed to make routes pay.
Cleaners already offered free pickup and delivery (1-800-DryClean, 2008); customers can go direct once they know the cleaner.

narrative.answer: PIVOT at **59**. Demand is real and the field is nearly empty, but outsourced cleaning plus a paid driver leaves about **17%** gross margin. Prove route density and pricing in one zip code before spending the seed round.
tldr: Mass, recurring need (~$22B US cleaning spend) and almost no app-first competitor before June 2013.
Outsourced model nets ~$4.51 per $26 order (estimate): margin dies if drivers do under 2 orders an hour.
Errand-delivery graveyard (MyLackey, Kozmo) and contractor-driver law (Estrada v. FedEx) are the warnings.

key_findings.title: Margin is thin after the driver
key_findings.detail: Est. **17%** gross margin per 15-lb order ($4.51 of $26.25) with LA couriers at $13.21/hr (BLS, 2011); at 1 order per driver-hour it falls to 2%.

key_findings.title: The errand-delivery graveyard is real
key_findings.detail: MyLackey, which picked up dry cleaning, burned **$8M in 16 months** and laid off 85 in 2000; Kozmo closed 9 markets in 2001.

key_findings.title: Open field, and smartphones are here
key_findings.detail: Only SpotlessCity ($200k seed, 3 NYC neighborhoods) found as a direct player, while **46%** of US adults owned a smartphone (Pew, 2012).

narrative.recommendation: Run a 7-day concierge pilot in one dense LA zip code; only build the full app and spend on ads if drivers hit **2+ orders per hour** at $6+ gross profit per order.
narrative.steelman: A $20B+ weekly need, 46% smartphone penetration and no funded app-first competitor in LA: an impulse purchase with Uber-style referral loops could own a city. The evidence backs demand and timing; it does not yet back the unit economics.

premortem.cause: Driver time per order kept contribution margin near zero, so growth burned the seed round.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 2 orders per driver-hour by week 3

premortem.cause: Customers went back to their cleaner's free delivery or their own washer after promo credits ran out.
premortem.early_signal: Under 30% of first-time customers reorder within 30 days

premortem.cause: A driver misclassification claim forced employee costs onto every order.
premortem.early_signal: Drivers working 30+ hours a week only for the platform, in branded gear

changes.what: US smartphone ownership rose from 35% to **46%** of adults in 9 months.
On-demand errand apps got venture funding (Exec, round led by Sam Altman).
Give-get referral credits became a proven launch channel (Uber personal promo codes).
Facebook ad clicks got cheaper: ~$0.55 average CPC in Q4 2012.

why_now.note: In 2000, MyLackey had no smartphones or cheap mobile ads; in 2013, both exist. The cost of a driver has not changed.

icp.who: Professionals aged 25-40 in dense LA neighborhoods (Santa Monica, West Hollywood, Downtown) who rent without in-unit washers and own smartphones (assumption)
where: Facebook ads targeted by zip code
icp.pays_for_today: Drop-off dry cleaning and wash & fold at local cleaners; dated 2012 LA prices unknown
icp.trigger: A busy week, a trip, or a suit needed for Monday morning

free_alternative.evidence: Searched DIY laundry, laundromats and cleaners' free delivery: they cover part of the job, but dry cleaning still needs a paid pro.

strong_competitor.evidence: Searched US laundry and dry-cleaning delivery players before June 2013: SpotlessCity raised only $200k; none showed $5M+ raised or 100k users.

graveyard.evidence: MyLackey (errands incl. dry-cleaning pickup) burned $8M in 16 months and laid off 85 (2000-10); Kozmo shut 9 markets (2001-04); Streamline closed.

no_distribution.evidence: Facebook CPC ~$0.55 (Q4 2012) / 2% conversion = ~$27.50 CAC, below est. first-year gross profit (~$108 at 2 orders/month); referrals work too.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Est. 17% gross margin: $26.25 order - $12.75 wholesale - $7.93 driver (LA courier $13.21/hr, BLS) - $1.06 card fees.

weak_demand.evidence: No dated pre-2013 trend for cleaning spend found; casual-dress decline sources were all published after 2013 and excluded.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Estrada v. FedEx Ground (CA Court of Appeal, 2007): contractor drivers held employees; review denied 2007-11. Contractor 'ninja' drivers face the same test.

saturated_wave.evidence: Searched look-alike launches 2012-06 to 2013-06: 0 confirmed (SpotlessCity launched 2012-01, before the window).

customer.segment: Urban professionals without in-unit washers in dense LA neighborhoods (assumption)
customer.pain: Cleaners' opening hours clash with work; laundry takes hours each week
customer.today: Drop-off at a local cleaner or laundromat, or own washer

Building amenity: pickup from apartment concierge

competitors.name: SpotlessCity
competitors.gap: NYC only, web-first, takes ~10% from cleaners

competitors.name: 1-800-DryClean
competitors.traction_note: Franchise expanding to Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Houston, DC (2011)
competitors.gap: Scheduled routes, not on-demand; no app

competitors.name: Exec
competitors.traction_note: YC W12, round led by Sam Altman; expanded into on-demand cleaning (2013-03)

competitors.name: Laundry Locker
competitors.gap: Self drop-off at lockers, no door pickup on demand

competitors.name: Do it yourself (own washer or laundromat)

scenarios.name: Pessimistic
scenarios.note: 2 orders/customer at 1 order per driver-hour: margin ~2%, burn ~$35k/month

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: Dry-cleaning mix, $2/lb, 3 orders/driver-hour: ~27% margin, small profit

risks.risk: Route density too low: driver time eats the margin
risks.mitigation: Fixed pickup windows, one zip code at a time

risks.risk: Contractor drivers reclassified as employees in California
risks.mitigation: Use courier firms or W-2 drivers; budget payroll costs

risks.risk: Customers bypass the app and use the partner cleaner's own delivery
risks.mitigation: Unbranded partner bags, exclusive partner deals

risks.risk: Lost or damaged garments with unclear liability between app and partner
risks.mitigation: Written partner liability terms and insurance

test_plan.step: Sign one partner cleaner in a dense LA zip code at a fixed wholesale rate per lb and per item
test_plan.verify: Signed rate sheet at or below $0.85/lb

test_plan.step: Launch a landing page with SMS ordering and a $5.99 delivery fee
Spend $300 on Facebook ads targeted at the zip code; flyer 2 apartment buildings
Founders run pickups in two fixed evening windows and log every minute
Compute gross profit per order and repeat intent
test_plan.verify: 30+ paid orders, $6+ gross profit per order

rescue.effort: 2-3 months of route and pricing tests
